name: toggle_bitplane_pixel
description: Flips one bit in a byte of bitplane memory, addressed by a base pointer plus an offset from a data register, with the bit number taken from another register. It then calls itself again, so the recovered code is a self-recursive stub.

name: skip_redundant_global_writes
description: Writes a shared global variable to itself three times, which has no effect, and then makes two calls to unnamed routines. Its only visible behaviour is those calls.

name: write_bitplane_pointer_table
description: Fills a four-entry table with pairs of address words, each entry one full bitplane (8000 bytes) further on than the last, with the copper-style move values advancing by four. It then makes two calls and stores a display control value in the shared global.

name: copy_words_to_fixed_buffer
description: Copies a block of words into a fixed buffer, writing every second slot, with the block length set by a power of two derived from a shared variable. It also loads a copper list pointer from a value computed from the same variable and writes a DMA control register.

name: halt_in_infinite_loop
description: Does nothing but loop forever, so the routine never returns. It behaves as a trap or a placeholder rather than working code.

name: enable_interrupt_channels
description: Stores a value, calls a routine, and then writes to the interrupt request and enable registers so that the master interrupt switch and the vertical blank interrupt are turned on. The routine returns the register values it was given.

name: call_through_stored_pointer
description: Calls the routine whose address is held in a shared global variable and returns the data register unchanged. It is an indirect dispatch point that lets callers choose the target through that variable.

name: run_blitter_and_wait
description: Waits until the blitter is idle, programs its control, modulo, pointer and size registers, and starts a blit by writing the size register. It then waits again until the blit has finished.

name: initialise_screen_and_seeds
description: Sets the background colour and DMA control, then waits in a loop until a shared flag clears. It then seeds three small counters from the random generator and makes a long chain of calls with fixed values before settling into an endless loop.

name: chain_two_subroutine_calls
description: Calls two routines one after the other with no other work in between. It is a thin wrapper that sequences those two steps.

name: wait_until_flag_set
description: Clears a shared flag and repeatedly calls a routine until that flag becomes nonzero. It is a busy-wait for an event that another routine signals.

name: seed_and_run_counted_loops
description: Resets the random seed to a fixed value and then runs three countdown loops whose lengths come from the counters set up earlier. The routine ends in invalid instruction data, so its final part cannot be recovered.

name: advance_random_and_divide
description: Advances a 32-bit linear congruential random state and divides its high word by a divisor passed in a register. It returns the quotient and the remainder.

name: advance_random_and_swap_halves
description: Advances the shared random state and returns the value with its two 16-bit halves swapped.

name: step_through_text_string
description: Checks a busy flag and, when it is idle, walks a zero-terminated string calling a per-character routine until the terminator is reached. At the end it resets a delay counter and toggles a flag.

name: output_string_and_count
description: Walks a zero-terminated string, passing each character to another routine and adding one to a shared counter for each character. It stops at the zero terminator.

name: call_and_increment_counter
description: Calls another routine and then adds one to a shared counter, returning the saved registers unchanged. It is called from two places.

name: decode_and_draw_text_character
description: Reads bytes from a message stream and handles a few control codes that set a delay, skip ahead, or move the cursor. Ordinary characters are mapped to a glyph index, drawn into the bitplanes with a shift, and the cursor advances by that glyph's width.

name: advance_frame_timers
description: Runs once per frame to advance several counters. It flips a phase flag every 32 ticks, toggles another flag on a fixed period, and counts down a timer while a shared state flag is set.

name: call_loader_with_fallback
description: Calls a function from a table supplied by the loader, and if that call fails it retries with a different setup. On the final path it writes a jump instruction into memory and jumps through a computed address; part of the control flow is unrecovered.

name: retry_disk_request_with_fallback
description: Calls a function from the loader's table to issue a disk request, and if that fails it fills in a request structure and retries with a second buffer address. If both attempts fail it writes a jump instruction into memory and transfers control through a computed address, and part of its control flow is unrecovered. It references the text 'disk.'.

name: dispatch_loader_request_by_index
description: When a selector value is nonzero, it stores a character derived from an index in a shared global and calls a loader-table function, returning that result if it succeeds. Otherwise it makes two other calls, toggles a bit in the shared global and returns zero.

name: apply_one_time_code_patches
description: On its first run, when a guard word still holds the original save-registers opcode, it overwrites that word and a block of nearby code with jump and move instructions that install replacement routines. It then calls one routine, applies a second patch step, and calls another routine.

name: apply_code_patch_if_unpatched
description: When a guard word still holds the original save-registers opcode, it overwrites that word and a nearby code location with a jump to a replacement routine. It then calls one routine and returns.

name: clear_sprite_pointer_registers
description: Writes zero to a run of consecutive longwords beginning at the first sprite pointer register, then sets a shared global variable to zero. It touches the DMA control register as well.

name: clear_sprite_pointer_registers
description: Writes zero to a run of consecutive longwords beginning at the first sprite pointer register, then sets a shared global variable to zero. It touches the DMA control register as well.

name: patch_load_sites_to_call
description: Checks two code words and, where each still holds a specific load opcode, overwrites it with a call instruction to a fixed routine. It is a small self-patching step with no other effect.

name: call_loader_table_entry
description: Calls one entry from the loader's function table and returns to its caller. It is a thin indirect call used by other routines in the same unit.

name: call_loader_if_nonzero
description: Calls a routine and, if the value it returns is nonzero, calls a loader-table entry. It passes the register pair through unchanged.

name: call_loader_if_nonzero
description: Calls a routine and, if the value it returns is nonzero, calls a loader-table entry. It passes the register pair through unchanged.

name: stub_undecompiled_save_entry
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code for this four-instruction routine. Its recorded facts show one call to another routine and a reference to the text 'MontyPythonsFC.save', and its address is taken as a value.

name: stub_undecompiled_save_text_user
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code for this nine-instruction routine. Its recorded facts show a reference to the text 'MontyPythonsFC.save' and that it is called from two places.

name: decode_keyboard_serial_byte
description: Rotates a shared byte into a new value and, when that value equals one specific keyboard code, replaces the stored byte with a fixed value. It returns the stored byte, and the facts show it works with the keyboard serial register.

name: set_flag_on_x_key
description: Checks whether the input byte is the character X and, if so, stores a fixed value in the shared global variable. It returns its stack argument unchanged.

name: allocate_and_read_boot_payload
description: Allocates a memory buffer through the system library and, if that succeeds, reads 2560 bytes from a fixed disk offset into it through the device library until the request completes. It then calls the first address of the buffer.

name: stub_returns_immediately
description: This routine is a single return with no other work, so it is a placeholder.

name: stub_undecompiled_dma_interrupt_setup
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code for this twelve-instruction routine. Its recorded facts show that it touches the DMA control and interrupt enable registers and makes one call.

name: stub_undecompiled_colour_routine
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code for this twelve-instruction routine. Its recorded facts show that it touches the background colour register and makes one call to another routine.

name: process_tile_index
description: Computes a tile index from an input word and a signed offset, using division and modulo by eleven and a flag taken from a second input. It repeatedly calls another routine to consume a bounded number of steps, updating a counter, and packs the result into a return word, or returns the input unchanged when the offset condition fails.

name: write_disk_sector_sync_marks
description: Loops over four units, clearing their words and writing the disk sync pattern and sync word into the track buffer when a shared flag is set. It calls a blitter wait routine and several other routines for each unit.

name: read_disk_track_with_retries
description: Makes up to five attempts at a disk read, setting the disk pointer, DMA and length registers on each attempt and calling another routine to wait for completion. It also selects a length value from a shared variable.

name: verify_sector_header_with_retries
description: Tries up to ten times to read a sector header, comparing the track and sector values with the expected ones. It returns zero when they match and a distinct error code otherwise.

name: verify_track_sector_values
description: Walks the eleven sectors of a track, waiting on a disk status bit and comparing values computed for each sector. It returns zero when all sectors agree and distinct error codes for a status failure or a mismatch.

name: stub_returns_immediately
description: Does nothing and returns, with no references to memory, registers or other routines, so it is an empty placeholder.

name: set_flag_and_increment_counter
description: Sets one bit in a 16-bit word that sits just before a pointer, with the bit number taken from a register, and then adds one to a 16-bit counter just before the same pointer.

name: clear_ten_strided_longwords
description: Writes zero to ten longwords spaced 272 bytes apart, starting at a pointer held in a register.

name: extract_high_byte_pair
description: Calls a routine for a 32-bit result and returns its low 16 bits in the upper half of the return value, with the top byte of the result in the lower half.

name: decode_mfm_long_pair
description: Takes two consecutive longwords, keeps the alternate bits of each, and combines them, with the second longword's bits in the lower position. This is the standard odd and even bit decode used for MFM-encoded disk data.

name: call_and_forward_result
description: Calls one routine, stores the value it returns, and passes that value as the argument to a second routine. It performs no other work.

name: compute_masked_xor_checksum
description: XORs ten consecutive longwords starting eight bytes past a pointer and returns the result masked to the alternate bits. This is the MFM-style checksum pattern used for encoded disk sectors.

name: compute_xor_checksum_by_length
description: XORs a run of longwords whose count is derived from a length argument, and returns the result masked to the alternate bits. It uses the same MFM-style checksum pattern as its neighbours.

name: fill_memory_with_pattern
description: Fills a block of 256 longwords with a fixed alternating bit pattern, starting from a pointer held in a shared variable.

name: initialize_object_state
description: Calls a routine and uses its result with two output registers to fill three integer fields of a structure. It then writes constant words into two fields and a derived word into a third.

name: set_object_transforms
description: Stores a sequence of values into fields of a structure, using results returned by other routines and several constant words. It also makes calls, one of which waits for the blitter.

name: reset_blitter_state
description: Waits for the blitter to be idle, then writes constants to its mask, modulo and data registers and to the DMA control register, and clears two shared globals.

name: update_bit7_after_two_calls
description: Calls two routines and then updates bit seven of a byte, using bit zero of the preceding byte as the flag. It sets bit seven when the flag is clear and bit six is also clear, clears it when the flag is set, and leaves the byte alone when the flag is clear and bit six is set.

name: update_bit7_from_flag_byte
description: Updates bit seven of a byte using bit zero of the preceding byte as the flag. It sets bit seven when the flag is clear and bit six is clear, clears it when the flag is set, and leaves the byte alone when the flag is clear and bit six is set.

name: start_disk_dma_transfer
description: Sets the disk sync word, the disk buffer pointer, the transfer length and the MFM control bits, then enables disk DMA. It starts a disk read or write transfer.

name: check_disk_ready_then_stop
description: Checks a device status bit once. If the bit is set it stops disk DMA and returns zero, otherwise it calls another routine and returns minus one.

name: reset_disk_length_register
description: Writes two values in turn to a shared location, so only the second value is kept. The facts show it touches the disk length and interrupt request registers.

name: write_adkcon_value_by_sign
description: Writes a fixed control value, and when a signed value in the caller's frame is negative it writes an all-ones value instead. The facts show it touches the audio and disk control register.

name: set_bit_in_global_flag
description: Sets one bit in a shared variable, with the bit number taken from a 16-bit value in the caller's frame plus three. The rest of the variable's value is kept.

name: set_global_ff_then_call
description: Writes an all-ones byte to a shared global and then calls two routines. The facts show it touches the CIAB port register.

name: update_table_entry
description: Reads a 16-bit entry from a table indexed by a value in the caller's frame and calls another routine when the entry is negative. It then loops for a count derived from the difference between two halves, writes a register value back into the table and calls another routine.

name: wait_then_clear_table_entry
description: Waits, calling another routine up to 56 times, for bit four of a shared variable to clear. When the bit clears it zeroes a table entry chosen by a frame value and returns zero, and otherwise it returns an error code after the last attempt.

name: read_ciab_port_status
description: Calls a routine to read a status value and clears one bit of it when a second returned value is nonnegative. It stores the result in a shared variable with its lowest bit forced on, then calls another routine. The facts show it touches the CIAB port register.

name: store_routine_result_global
description: Calls a routine and stores its return value in a shared global variable, with no other work.

name: update_ciab_prb_bit
description: Builds a byte from a shared variable with one bit cleared, the bit chosen by a frame value plus three, and clears a further bit when a table entry is odd. It returns the byte as the register result.

name: wait_for_flag_and_result
description: Repeatedly calls a routine and waits for the lowest bit of a shared flag to clear between calls, stopping once the routine returns one. It then returns zero.

name: write_sequence_if_flag_clear
description: When the lowest bit of a shared flag is clear and the input is not one, it writes three control values to a shared variable in turn. Otherwise it does nothing.

name: write_three_control_values
description: Writes three fixed byte values to a shared variable in turn and returns. The facts show it touches the CIA timer registers.

name: stub_undecompiled_runtime_entry
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code for this 68-instruction routine. Its recorded facts show that it makes four calls to unnamed routines.

name: chain_four_routine_calls
description: Calls four unnamed routines one after another and returns, with no other work.

name: chain_four_routine_calls
description: Calls four unnamed routines one after another and returns, with no other work.

name: chain_two_subroutine_calls
description: Calls two unnamed routines one after another and returns, with no other work.

name: clear_global_then_call
description: Clears a shared global, makes one call into the executable, and then calls another routine. It returns with no other work.

name: run_setup_then_pointer_list
description: Makes several setup calls, clears a shared global, and then walks a list of addresses ending in minus one, calling a stored function and another routine for each entry.

name: call_each_pointer_list_entry
description: Walks a list of addresses ending in minus one, calling a stored function and another routine for each entry. It returns its stack argument unchanged.

name: call_two_routines_per_entry
description: Walks a list of values ending in minus one and calls two routines for each entry. It returns its input register values unchanged.

name: mix_two_word_state
description: Shifts a pair of registers left by three bits and XORs the second word with a value derived from the shifted bits, then moves the first word into the second slot. It updates a two-word shared state in place.

name: forward_through_jump_vector
description: Calls a jump-table entry that passes control straight on to a fixed address, then returns its input register values unchanged. It is a thin pass-through wrapper.

name: forward_through_jump_vector
description: Calls a jump-table entry that passes control straight on to a fixed address, then returns its input register values unchanged. It is a thin pass-through wrapper.

name: toggle_bit_and_mask_bytes
description: Toggles one bit in a byte addressed by a pointer, with the bit number taken from a register, and clears a byte just before the pointer. It then masks another byte with a fixed pattern. The routine ends in invalid instruction data, so its tail is unrecovered.

name: skip_redundant_global_writes
description: Writes a shared global variable to itself twice, which has no effect, so the routine does nothing useful.

name: disable_interrupts_then_clear_block
description: Writes a value with bit fifteen clear to the interrupt and DMA control registers, which disables them, then zeroes a very large block of memory in a single loop. It also sets two shared variables to the same fixed value.

name: store_doubled_value_pair
description: Doubles a 16-bit input value and stores the result in two shared variables, one of which is a fixed location.

name: copy_table_words_to_destinations
description: Copies thirty words from a source table, selected through a shared index, into the addresses listed starting at a shared variable. It returns its input register unchanged.

name: copy_fixed_table_to_destinations
description: Copies thirty words from a fixed source table into the addresses listed starting at a shared variable. It returns its input register unchanged.

name: setup_display_window_registers
description: Writes constants to the display window, data fetch, bitplane modulo and bitplane control state, and clears some shared variables. It then makes one call and a call to another routine.

name: reset_shared_state_variables
description: Sets one shared flag to all ones, sets two shared variables to fifteen, clears two others, and makes one call to another routine.

name: reset_display_window_defaults
description: Writes default values to the display window, data fetch and bitplane modulo state variables and clears a flag. It then makes a call to another routine.

name: set_flag_and_reset_state
description: Sets one shared flag to one, sets two shared variables to fifteen, clears two others, and makes one call to another routine.

name: configure_alternate_display_window
description: Writes a second layout of display window, data fetch and bitplane control values and clears a shared flag. It makes one call to another routine.

name: store_routine_address
description: Stores the address of a routine in a shared global variable, with no other work.

name: run_counter_step_sequence
description: Increments a shared counter, calls two routines, copies a saved value back into the counter, calls another routine, and then sets the counter to a fixed value. The facts show it touches the background colour and interrupt request registers.

name: halt_in_infinite_loop
description: The recovered body is an endless loop with no work, so the routine never returns. The calls recorded for it do not appear in the recovered body.

name: halt_in_infinite_loop
description: The recovered body is an endless loop with no work, so the routine never returns. The calls recorded for it do not appear in the recovered body.

name: forward_single_routine_call
description: Calls one routine and returns, with no other work.

name: select_alternating_nibble_pattern
description: Toggles a phase bit in a shared flag, selects one of two shared 16-bit values according to that bit, and stores the inverted low nibble repeated in both halves of a byte. It returns its register values unchanged.

name: set_dma_and_interrupt_control
description: Writes three fixed values to the DMA control, interrupt request and interrupt enable registers, enabling or clearing the channels and interrupts that the bits name.

name: initialize_blitter_registers
description: Writes constant values to the blitter control registers and to the first and last word mask registers, then clears two shared variables. The facts show it also touches the DMA control register.

name: stub_undecompiled_single_instruction
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code for this single-instruction routine, and the facts record no calls, registers or text. Nothing more can be said from the evidence.

name: forward_single_routine_call
description: Calls one routine and returns, with no other work.

name: copy_doubled_words_to_globals
description: Copies sixteen words from a source pointer into a block of shared variables, doubling each value on the way. It returns its input register values unchanged.

name: return_constant_from_callee
description: Makes one call to a one-instruction routine that loads a fixed value into the data register, then returns that register.

name: return_result_of_call
description: Calls one routine and returns the data register unchanged. It is a thin wrapper that passes the call's result through.

name: clear_four_plane_longword_rows
description: Zeroes ten groups of longwords in four areas spaced 8192 bytes apart, repeating for a count held in the data register.

name: return_result_of_call
description: Calls one routine and returns the data register unchanged. It is a thin wrapper that passes the call's result through.

name: return_result_of_call
description: Calls one routine and returns the data register unchanged. It is a thin wrapper that passes the call's result through.

name: start_blitter_block_copy
description: When the row count is positive, it programs the blitter control, modulo and pointer registers from two addresses offset by a fixed amount, then starts a blit whose size combines the count with a fixed row field. It does nothing when the count is not positive.

name: stub_returns_immediately
description: Does nothing and returns, with no references to memory, registers or other routines, so it is an empty placeholder.

name: copy_listed_blocks_to_buffer
description: Walks a list of entries ending at a terminator byte, capped at forty entries. For each entry it copies eight rows from four source planes spaced 8192 bytes apart into a destination buffer.

name: store_input_word_global
description: Stores a 16-bit input value into a shared counter variable and returns its stack argument unchanged.

name: copy_indexed_entries_to_planes
description: Walks a list of indexes ending at a 255 terminator. For each index it copies a 32-byte table entry into four bitplane regions spaced 8192 bytes apart.

name: clear_region_and_walk_list
description: Clears a region of 200 rows across four areas spaced 8192 bytes apart, then walks a list of entries with another routine, stopping when the routine result is not positive. It returns its input registers unchanged.

name: clear_region_and_walk_list
description: Clears a region of 200 rows across four areas spaced 8192 bytes apart, then walks a list of entries with another routine, stopping when the routine result is not positive. It returns its input registers unchanged.

name: walk_counted_list_entries
description: Walks a list of count-prefixed entries, calling another routine repeatedly for each count, and stops when the routine result is not positive or a terminator is reached. It returns its input registers unchanged.

name: copy_entry_planes_swapped
description: Copies one 32-byte table entry into four bitplane regions spaced 8192 bytes apart. When a flag bit is set, it first swaps two particular index values.

name: copy_entry_to_planes_remap
description: Copies one 32-byte table entry into four bitplane regions spaced 8192 bytes apart, first mapping index twenty to nineteen.

name: configure_cia_interrupt_mask
description: Stores a routine address in one shared variable and writes a fixed control value to the CIA interrupt control register. It returns its byte argument unchanged.

name: handle_cia_timer_event
description: When a flag bit is set it calls another routine, stores a rotated and inverted copy of its byte result, and reprograms CIA control, timer and interrupt values. Otherwise it only writes a control value. The facts show it touches the CIA timer and interrupt registers.

name: write_cia_control_value
description: Writes a fixed control value to a CIA register, after a conditional write of the same value that depends on bit zero of the input.

name: decode_input_state
description: Reads the joystick and mouse movement registers and the fire button bit, then turns them into direction and button flags stored in shared variables. It returns its register inputs unchanged.

name: reset_audio_channel_state
description: Clears the audio channel state variables and writes zero volume to the four audio channels. The facts also show it touches the DMA and interrupt enable registers.

name: update_channel_state_machine
description: Looks up a per-channel table entry and, depending on its value, either sets or clears bits in a state byte, or runs a rotating two-bit sequence. It then calls other routines and clears a counter.

name: run_channel_routines_if_active
description: Calls one routine, then when a shared state value is nonzero makes one or two further calls, depending on a flag. It returns with no further work when the state value is zero.

name: store_routine_address
description: Stores the address of a routine in a shared global variable and returns its byte argument unchanged.

name: process_flagged_channel_entries
description: Walks four channel structures from the highest to the lowest. For each one whose bit is set in the input word, it checks a status flag and, when appropriate, sets status bits, copies a field into a shared variable and records a value.

name: update_channel_entries_by_mask
description: Walks a list of channel structures, using a bit mask from a register to select entries. For each selected entry it sets a status bit and stores fixed words, looping until the list is exhausted.

name: initialize_channel_tables_from_index
description: Uses the low byte of the data register to select three channel pointers from a table, sets their state fields, and fills three blocks with an incrementing byte pattern in steps of fourteen. It finishes by writing a terminator byte.

name: advance_sequence_command_stream
description: Steps a byte-coded command stream for a channel. When a counter reaches zero it reads the next command, which may set a value, set a length, end the stream or select a target, and otherwise it calls other routines each step.

name: set_byte_flag_to_one
description: Writes the value one to the byte that the address register points to.

name: step_channel_command_stream
description: Advances one channel's command stream: it decrements a counter, reads the next command when the counter reaches zero, applies set-value and length commands, and calls other routines. It returns the value of the last routine.

name: decode_stream_command_byte
description: Decodes one command byte from a stream. A byte in one high range loads a value from a table, 255 marks the stream as finished, and a byte in another range stores a four-bit field. Other bytes are ignored.

name: step_channel_duration_counter
description: Steps a channel's duration counter: it counts down a field, reads the next byte from the stream when the count expires, and returns a value looked up from a table. A flag bit makes it return the stored value directly.

name: initialize_channel_structure
description: Initialises a channel structure from a source record: it stores a pointer, copies two word fields, sets state flags and loads a word from the source record into a shared variable pair. The facts show it touches the DMA and interrupt registers.

name: stub_undecompiled_channel_callee
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code for this seven-instruction routine. The facts show one call and one caller, and nothing else.

name: stub_undecompiled_dma_status_check
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code for this seventeen-instruction routine. The facts show it reads the DMA control status register and has one caller.

name: stub_undecompiled_runtime_block
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code for this twenty-six-instruction routine, and the facts record no calls, registers or text. Only its size is known.

name: stub_returns_immediately
description: Does nothing and returns, with no references to memory, registers or other routines, so it is an empty placeholder.

name: setup_display_copy_and_jump

It then patches a call instruction, makes several calls and jumps to the copied code at a fixed low address. It references the text names Arkanoid.1 to Arkanoid.3.

name: xor_scramble_block_if_ok
description: Calls a loader-table entry and, when that call succeeds, makes two further calls and XORs 230 bytes starting at a shared variable with a decreasing counter. It returns 230 when the block is scrambled and zero otherwise. It references the text 'highs'.

name: call_loader_entry_between_steps
description: Calls one routine, then a loader-table entry at a fixed offset, then another routine. It returns with no other work.

name: xor_scramble_global_block
description: XORs 230 bytes starting at a shared variable with a decreasing counter and returns 230. It references the text 'highs'.

name: xor_fixed_block_if_ok
description: Calls a loader-table entry and, when that call succeeds, makes two further calls and XORs 230 bytes at a fixed address with a decreasing counter, returning 230. It returns zero when the first call fails.

name: call_loader_entry_between_steps
description: Calls one routine, then a loader-table entry at a fixed offset, then another routine. It returns with no other work.

name: xor_scramble_fixed_block
description: XORs 230 bytes starting at a fixed address with a decreasing counter and returns 230. It references the text 'highs'.

name: repeat_call_count_times
description: Calls one routine as many times as the count in the input word, counting down to zero.

name: repeat_call_while_counter_within
description: Calls a routine repeatedly, counting up from one until the counter passes the value that routine returns.

name: fade_palette_by_ratio
description: Scales each 4-bit colour component of a source table by a ratio, dividing by a value from another routine, and writes the results to the colour registers in turn. It stops when its count reaches zero.

name: wait_for_flag_edge
description: Waits for the lowest bit of a shared variable to become set and then clear again, so it waits for one complete change of that flag. The facts show it also touches a custom chip register.

name: step_object_toward_target
description: Moves an object one step toward a target coordinate, consulting a grid of lookup tables to test for blocked cells and set movement flags. It then checks a table of records against the position and marks any record it hits.

name: check_record_hits_in_window
description: Walks three records and checks the input position against each record's horizontal and vertical window. When a match is found and the record's bit is set in a mask, it marks the record and calls another routine.

name: append_record_to_bounded_buffer
description: Appends a record to a bounded buffer that wraps back to a fixed start address at its end, choosing one of three record layouts from a flag value. It then calls other routines.

name: append_record_with_flag_check
description: Writes one record into the same bounded buffer, with a layout that depends on a flag value. It calls other routines when a flag bit allows it.

name: write_record_with_routine_calls
description: Writes a record into a fixed buffer layout chosen by a flag, makes three calls to other routines, and makes a fourth when a count is small and a flag bit is clear. It updates the buffer pointer.

name: write_plain_record_then_calls
description: Writes a two-word record at an offset from a base address, advances a buffer pointer, and makes three calls to other routines. A fourth call is made when a count is small and a flag bit is clear.

name: copy_tile_rows_to_planes
description: Blanks a set of rows in four bitplane areas, then copies eight words from a source table into each of four destination rows. The destination uses a 42-byte row stride and the source a 26-byte stride.

name: clear_tile_column_in_planes
description: Clears a column of eight row groups across the bitplane areas, with the start address computed from a shared value and a register and a 26-byte row stride.

name: compute_table_derived_fields
description: Negates and masks a 16-bit value, looks up a scaled entry and two further table fields from it, and stores the results in fields of a structure. It returns a packed value with the high bits cleared.

name: set_limit_flags_if_exceeded
description: Compares two input values against limits and, when one is exceeded, sets a status word and flag bits in a structure. It has a separate branch for each limit.

name: set_nonpositive_limit_flags
description: Sets a status flag and flag bits in a structure when the first input is zero or less, and does the same with a second flag when the second input is zero or less.

name: set_upper_limit_flag
description: Sets a status flag and a flag word in a structure when a value reaches a limit.

name: set_lower_limit_flag
description: Sets a status flag and a flag word in a structure when a value is zero or less.

name: copy_block_groups_to_planes
description: Copies blocks of words from a source record into four bitplane areas spaced 8192 bytes apart, in one of two passes chosen by a flag, and calls 24 other routines. Only the first part of its pseudo-code was available, so this covers that part.

name: advance_stepped_sequence
description: Advances a stepped sequence record: once its delay counter expires, it reads the next value from a list, updates direction and step fields, and calls a function pointer for each step until the count runs out.

name: run_stepped_callbacks_then_store
description: Walks a count of steps, calling a function pointer on each one and adjusting a value by a fixed step, with a wrap at 2048 units depending on a flag. It then stores the final values back into the record.

name: initialize_record_from_tables
description: Sets up a record from two tables indexed by a register, calls a list of routine routines, and waits on the raster position before finishing. It enables DMA through the DMA control register.

name: build_cell_entry_list
description: Clears a fixed buffer and then scans a grid of table words, writing a three-word entry for each cell whose flag bit is set, with a type code chosen by the flag pattern.

name: scan_cells_and_emit_entries
description: Scans a grid of table words and, for each flagged cell, marks it and calls other routines to emit entries. It runs in one of two modes chosen by a flag.

name: decode_run_length_rows
description: Fills a table of row pointers, then decodes a run-length list into a buffer, where a negative count repeats the following value and a non-negative count copies literal words.

name: copy_flagged_tile_rows
description: When a bit in a table word is set, copies a group of eight rows from a source table into a destination area with a 42-byte row stride. It makes one call to another routine.

name: copy_flagged_tile_rows_extended
description: Like its neighbour, copies a group of eight rows from a source table when a table bit is set, and writes one extra column for each row.

name: call_routine_per_record
description: Walks a list of six-word records while the first two fields are nonzero, calling a routine for each record.

name: chain_two_subroutine_calls
description: Calls two unnamed routines one after another and returns, with no other work.

name: chain_two_subroutine_calls
description: Calls two unnamed routines one after another and returns, with no other work.

name: call_if_field_range_one
description: Calls a routine only when a shared field lies between one and five inclusive.

name: call_if_field_range_two
description: Calls a routine only when a shared field lies between two and six inclusive.

name: call_pairs_by_clamped_count
description: Clamps a shared count to six, then calls two routines for each step of a loop that runs the count minus two times, when the count is above one.

name: keep_high_byte_of_word
description: Writes the low byte and then the high byte of a shared word into the same location, so the high byte is what remains. It returns its register inputs unchanged.

name: advance_timed_state
description: Advances a timed state variable by a step returned from another routine. When a threshold is passed it sets a state bit, calls other routines and resets two fields to fixed values.

name: select_highest_active_record
description: Scans eight records and chooses the one with the largest second field below 200 among those whose bit is set in a mask. It stores an offset derived from that record and sets a shared flag from one bit of the input.

name: compute_absolute_motion_deltas
description: Reads a shared input state and computes the absolute difference between the previous and current values on two axes, returning both as a pair. The facts show it reads the fire button port and the mouse movement register.

name: allocate_free_record_slot
description: Looks for a free slot among two records using a bit mask, sets that slot's bit, fills in its two fields from shared values, and returns a pointer to it. It returns null when both slots are in use.

name: claim_slot_and_initialise_pair
description: When the input index is below two and its bit is set in a mask, it marks the slot as taken, decrements a shared count and initialises two records for that slot. It returns zero on success and minus one otherwise.

name: update_position_with_threshold
description: When a record's flag is clear, it calls another routine and then sets a second record's position field from a shared value. It also sets a flag bit and adjusts the position when the value falls within a threshold.

name: start_entry_if_idle
description: When the input index is below eight and two shared flags are clear, it marks a state byte, stores four input values and calls other routines, returning zero. Otherwise it returns minus one.

name: mark_entry_if_flagged
description: When a shared flag byte is nonzero, it sets another state byte to all ones and returns zero. Otherwise it returns minus one.

name: set_position_from_offset
description: Clears a field, calls another routine and, if that field is still zero, sets a position value to a stored offset plus the input.

name: dispatch_state_handler
description: Depending on a shared state value other than minus one, calls up to three routines and then dispatches through a table of handlers. It then resets the state to minus one.

name: set_flag_bytes_to_ones
description: Sets two byte flags to all ones and writes one to a shared variable.

name: chain_four_routine_calls
description: Calls four unnamed routines one after another and returns, with no other work.

name: reset_record_flags
description: Clears a shared variable and then, for seven records, sets a status field to one wherever it is currently nonzero.

name: clear_record_if_active
description: When a shared pointer is nonzero, writes a fixed value into two fields of the record it points to, then clears the pointer.

name: clear_record_if_active
description: When a shared pointer is nonzero, writes a fixed value into two fields of the record it points to, then clears the pointer.

name: set_flag_and_clear_global
description: Writes all ones into a byte field of a record and clears a shared variable.

name: initialise_slot_record_with_ratios
description: When an index below eight is unused, it marks the slot as taken, stores position and speed fields, computes two quotient and remainder pairs by dividing by a shared count, and calls another routine. It returns zero when the slot is used or out of range.

name: release_slot_and_count_down
description: When an index below eight is in use, it marks a flag bit and decrements a shared count. When the count reaches zero it adds two to a field and calls another routine, returning zero on success and minus one otherwise.
